steps.title: Use the known root x = 2 to get a factor

lines.text: $A(2,0)$ is on the graph, so $x = 2$ is a root and $(x-2)$ is a factor.
B and C are where $f(x) = 0$. Split $f(x)$ so that every group contains $(x-2)$.
$x = 2$ is point $A$, so $B$ and $C$ have $x = 4.5$ and $x = 7$ (B is left of C on the graph). Their $y$-coordinate is $0$.
Since $f(-3) = 0$, $x = -3$ is a root and $(x+3)$ is a factor.

$z = -\sqrt{3} + i$ is in the second quadrant (negative real part, positive imaginary part). Find the reference angle $\alpha$ first.
$[r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)]^n = r^n(\cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta)$.
$\frac{10\pi}{3} - 2\pi = \frac{4\pi}{3}$, which is in the third quadrant, so both values are negative.
The point $\sqrt{3} - i$ has real part $\sqrt{3}$ and imaginary part $-1$.
The point is in the fourth quadrant, so measure the reference angle and subtract it from $360^\circ$.
$[r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)]^n = r^n(\cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta)$.
$2970^\circ - 8 \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ$, so $\cos 2970^\circ = 0$ and $\sin 2970^\circ = 1$.
